Plan: Budget Service (backend + frontend + terraform)

Context

A Budget entity and stub controller/service/repository already exist inside alerts-service, but the user wants a standalone budget-service. lb.tf currently routes /api/v1/budgets* to alerts-service — that path needs to move to the new
service. The frontend has no budgets page at all.

 ---
1. New service — services/budget-service/

Copy the structure of services/expense-service/. Key deviations:
- Port 8089
- No shared-schema User FK — use a plain userId UUID field on the Budget entity (avoids having to manage the users table in migrations)
- No SSE, no versioning/optimistic locking — plain CRUD is enough

Files to create

settings.gradle

rootProject.name = 'budget-service'

build.gradle

Copy services/expense-service/build.gradle verbatim, change rootProject.name reference and remove any SSE/event dependencies if present. Keep: JPA, Validation, Web, OAuth2 Resource Server, Flyway (PostgreSQL), SpringDoc, Lombok, PostgreSQL
driver, Testcontainers.

Dockerfile

Copy services/expense-service/Dockerfile. Change expense-service → budget-service in COPY and WORKDIR lines.

src/main/resources/application.properties

Copy expense-service's properties. Change:
- spring.application.name=budget-service
- server.port=8089
- spring.datasource.hikari.pool-name=${DB_POOL_NAME:budget-service-hikari}

src/main/resources/db/migration/V1__create_budgets.sql

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS budgets (
id          UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
user_id     UUID NOT NULL,
category    TEXT NOT NULL,
limit_amount NUMERIC(12, 2) NOT NULL CHECK (limit_amount > 0),
period      TEXT NOT NULL
);
IF NOT EXISTS makes it safe on a database where shared-schema already created the table — Flyway will record V1 as applied regardless.

Java package: com.spendmart.budget_service

BudgetServiceApplication.java — standard @SpringBootApplication main class.

config/SecurityConfig.java
Copy from services/expense-service/.../config/SecurityConfig.java. Change the permitted health path to /api/v1/budgets/health.

GlobalExceptionHandler.java
Copy from services/expense-service/.../GlobalExceptionHandler.java unchanged — same error codes apply.

dto/BudgetRequest.java
Copy from services/alerts-service/.../dto/BudgetRequest.java — already has @NotBlank on category/period, @NotNull @Positive on limitAmount.

dto/BudgetResponse.java — new:
public record BudgetResponse(UUID id, String category, BigDecimal limitAmount, String period) {}

entity/Budget.java — local entity (NOT shared-schema):
@Entity @Table(name = "budgets")
@Data @NoArgsConstructor @AllArgsConstructor @Builder
public class Budget {
@Id @GeneratedValue(strategy = GenerationType.UUID)
private UUID id;
@Column(name = "user_id", nullable = false)
private UUID userId;
@Column(nullable = false) private String category;
@Column(name = "limit_amount", nullable = false, precision = 12, scale = 2)
private BigDecimal limitAmount;
@Column(nullable = false) private String period;
}

repository/BudgetRepository.java
Based on alerts-service stub:
public interface BudgetRepository extends JpaRepository<Budget, UUID> {
List<Budget> findByUserId(UUID userId);
}

service/BudgetService.java
Implement the four CRUD methods. Pattern from alerts-service stub + expense-service style:
- create(UUID userId, BudgetRequest req) → save and return BudgetResponse
- getByUser(UUID userId) → List<BudgetResponse>
- update(UUID userId, UUID budgetId, BudgetRequest req) → find by id, verify userId matches, update fields, save
- delete(UUID userId, UUID budgetId) → find by id, verify userId matches, delete

Throw EntityNotFoundException (404) if budget not found, ForbiddenException (403) if userId doesn't match.

controller/BudgetController.java
Based on alerts-service stub controller, completed:
- POST /api/v1/budgets → create
- GET /api/v1/budgets → getByUser
- PUT /api/v1/budgets/{budgetId} → update
- DELETE /api/v1/budgets/{budgetId} → delete (returns 204)
- GET /api/v1/budgets/health → 200 OK (unauthenticated)

Extract userId from @AuthenticationPrincipal Jwt jwt → UUID.fromString(jwt.getSubject()).

 ---
2. Terraform

terraform/lb.tf

- Remove "/api/v1/budgets*" from alerts-service paths (so it only has "/api/v1/alerts*")
- Add new entry:
  "budget-service" = { port = 8089, paths = ["/api/v1/budgets*"], health_path = "/api/v1/budgets/health", priority = 70 }

terraform/ecr.tf

Add "budget-service" to the service_names local list.

terraform/ecs.tf

1. Add "budget-service" = 8089 to the internal_services locals map.
2. Add aws_ecs_task_definition.budget_service — copy pattern from expense_service, port 8089, env vars SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL, COGNITO_JWKS_URI, secrets for DB username/password.
3. Add aws_ecs_service.budget_service — copy pattern from expense_service, wire to target group and Cloud Map.

 ---
3. Frontend

frontend/budgets.html

New page following the groups.html layout:
- Two cards: "Add Budget" form + "Your Budgets" table
- Form fields: Category (text), Limit Amount (number), Period (select: MONTHLY/WEEKLY)
- Table columns: Category | Period | Limit | Actions (Edit, Delete)
- <p id="status" class="status" hidden></p>
- <script type="module" src="./assets/js/pages/budgets.js"></script>
- Sidebar data-page="budgets" active on the Banking nav section (or add a new Account entry)

frontend/assets/js/pages/budgets.js

Follow groups.js pattern:
- nav('budgets') on load
- loadBudgets() → api.get('/budgets') → render table
- Create button → api.post('/budgets', {category, limitAmount, period}) → reload
- Edit (inline or prompt) → api.put('/budgets/{id}', {...}) → reload
- Delete button → api.del('/budgets/{id}') → reload

❯ is there a way to look through the whole project and generate an API spec. Not using AI but some sort of plugin or tool

● It's already set up — every service has springdoc-openapi-starter-webmvc-ui:2.8.9 in build.gradle and these properties configured:

springdoc.api-docs.path=/api-docs
springdoc.swagger-ui.path=/swagger-ui.html

SpringDoc scans your @RestController annotations at startup and generates an OpenAPI 3.0 spec automatically. When any service is running you get:

- http://localhost:<port>/api-docs — raw JSON spec
- http://localhost:<port>/swagger-ui.html — interactive Swagger UI

So for example with expense-service on 8082: http://localhost:8082/api-docs.

For a combined spec across all services, there's no single tool that does it out of the box since they're separate processes. Your options:

1. Collect at runtime — hit each /api-docs endpoint and merge the JSONs with a tool like swagger-merger or openapi-merge-cli
2. Generate without running — use the springdoc-openapi-maven-plugin, which spins up the app during the Maven/Gradle build and dumps the spec to a file. Would need a small Gradle task added to each service's build.gradle
3. API gateway aggregation — if you front everything with something like Kong or AWS API Gateway, they can aggregate specs automatically

The easiest for your setup right now is option 1 — start your services locally and run openapi-merge-cli pointing at each /api-docs URL. Want me to set that up?

● The error is:
Found non-empty schema(s) "public" but no schema history table.

Flyway sees your DB already has tables but no flyway_schema_history tracking table — so it refuses to run. This happens when tables exist (from a previous setup or docker init) but Flyway has never run against this DB before.

The fix is one line in application.properties — add spring.flyway.baseline-on-migrate=true. This tells Flyway "treat whatever's already in the DB as baseline V0 and proceed from there."

● Let me check the banking service code to understand where that transaction comes from.

Searched for 2 patterns, read 3 files (ctrl+o to expand)

● That transaction was already in the BankAPI Node.js service — you didn't insert it. Here's how I can tell:

1. The id UUID changes on every request — BankApiAdapter.toNormalised() calls UUID.randomUUID() each time, so it's generated fresh per call, never persisted. You can see this in your terminal: each curl hit returned a different id for the
   same underlying transaction.
2. The externalTxnId stays the same (6a2174895cd3a5acd73d5c7d) — that's the real ID coming from the BankAPI Node.js service, which looks like a MongoDB ObjectId. That's the seed/test data that was already loaded in the BankAPI container.
3. The only thing you inserted was a row into the PostgreSQL users table (local@test.com) so the banking service had a valid user to associate transactions with.

So the flow is: your POST /login/bankapi call authenticates against the BankAPI Node.js service → banking-service fetches that pre-existing NGN 5000 transaction from BankAPI → wraps it with a fresh UUID and your userId each time.

● Now I have a complete picture. Here's the analysis:

What BankApiNodeJs exposes:
- POST /api/login → returns full user object with token (JWT containing user_id) and accountNumber
- GET /api/user/:Id → returns user object (no auth required)
- GET /api/transaction/:accountNumber → returns transaction array (no auth required)

What exists in banking-service:
- BankApiAdapter — stub with providerKey() = "bankapi" that returns List.of() (TODO)
- BankAuthClient already fetches the stored BankApiNodeJs JWT via bankAuthClient.getToken(cognitoJwt, "bankapi")

The gap: BankApiAdapter.fetchTransactions() needs to:
1. Decode the stored JWT to extract user_id
2. Call GET /api/user/{user_id} → get accountNumber
3. Call GET /api/transaction/{accountNumber} → get transactions, map to NormalisedTransaction

Login response (POST /api/login):
{
"_id": "6a21747a5cd3a5acd73d5c78",

Transaction response (GET /api/transaction/:accountNumber):

"transactionType": "Deposit",

"sender": "External",

What needs wiring in banking-service (BankApiAdapter):

1. The stored JWT payload contains user_id (MongoDB _id) — decode it to call GET /api/user/{user_id} and get accountNumber
2. Call GET /api/transaction/{accountNumber} — no auth header needed, it's a public endpoint
3. Map transactionAmount → amount, "NGN" for currency, transactionTime → occurredAt, _id → externalTxnId

The key insight: bank-auth-service already has BankApiNodeJsClient that calls /api/login and extracts the token field — but the login response also includes accountNumber. We could either store that in bank-auth-service as a composite value,
or decode the JWT in BankApiAdapter to get the user's MongoDB _id and fetch the user from /api/user/:Id to get the account number.

Plan: Deploy BankApiNodeJs to ECS and Wire banking-service

Context

BankApiNodeJs is a Node.js/Express/MongoDB bank API that the team wants to run as an ECS Fargate service. The banking-service already has a BankApiAdapter stub (providerKey = "bankapi") that returns an empty list — it needs to be wired to
call BankApiNodeJs for real transaction data. The bank-auth-service already calls BankApiNodeJs for login (BankApiNodeJsClient + /api/v1/login/bankapi endpoint) and stores the returned JWT in DynamoDB. The flow already works end-to-end
locally — this plan gets it running in ECS.

 ---
Architecture

User → ALB → bank-auth-service (8087)
↓ POST /api/login → bank-api-nodejs:3000
↓ stores JWT in DynamoDB keyed (userId, "bankapi")

User → ALB → banking-service (8083)
↓ GET /api/v1/token/bankapi → bank-auth-service (fetches JWT)
↓ BankApiAdapter.fetchTransactions(token)
↓ decode JWT → extract user_id
↓ GET /api/user/{user_id}   → bank-api-nodejs:3000
↓ GET /api/transaction/{accountNumber} → bank-api-nodejs:3000

bank-api-nodejs is internal-only — no ALB routing needed. Cloud Map gives it a stable DNS name: bank-api-nodejs.spendsmart.local:3000.

 ---
Part 1 — Move BankApiNodeJs into the services directory

Move BankApiNodeJs/ → services/bank-api-nodejs/ so it sits alongside the other services and matches the Terraform build-context path (../services/{name}).

services/bank-api-nodejs/
app.js
index.js
package.json
package-lock.json
config/database.js
controllers/userController.js
middleware/auth.js
models/transaction.js
models/user.js
routes/bankApiRoutes.js
Dockerfile          ← new
.dockerignore       ← new

Remove the nested .git directory so it becomes part of the main repo.

 ---
Part 2 — BankApiNodeJs app changes

2a. Add /health endpoint

ECS requires a health check. Add before the catch-all 404 in index.js:
app.get('/health', (req, res) => res.status(200).json({ status: 'ok' }));

2b. Create services/bank-api-nodejs/Dockerfile

FROM node:20-alpine
WORKDIR /app
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci --only=production
COPY . .
EXPOSE 3000
CMD ["node", "index.js"]

2c. Create services/bank-api-nodejs/.dockerignore

node_modules
.env
.git

 ---
Part 3 — Terraform changes

3a. terraform/ecr.tf — add to service_names

locals {
service_names = [
"expense-service",
"banking-service",
"query-service",
"alerts-service",
"bank-auth-service",
"group-service",
"bank-api-nodejs",   # ← add
]
}
This automatically creates: ECR repo, Docker image build/push, CloudWatch log group, log_config entry.

3b. terraform/ecs.tf — add to internal_services and add task definition + service

Add to local.internal_services:
"bank-api-nodejs" = 3000
This creates the Cloud Map DNS entry: bank-api-nodejs.spendsmart.local.

Add a new Secrets Manager secret reference local for the MongoDB URI and BankApi token key:
bank_api_mongo_uri_secret  = "${aws_secretsmanager_secret.bank_api.arn}:mongo_uri::"
bank_api_token_key_secret  = "${aws_secretsmanager_secret.bank_api.arn}:token_key::"

Add a new aws_secretsmanager_secret.bank_api resource in terraform/secrets.tf (or ecs.tf) to hold MONGO_URI and TOKEN_KEY.

Add ECS task definition:
resource "aws_ecs_task_definition" "bank_api_nodejs" {
family                   = "spendsmart-bank-api-nodejs"
network_mode             = "awsvpc"
requires_compatibilities = ["FARGATE"]
cpu                      = 256
memory                   = 512
execution_role_arn       = data.aws_iam_role.lab.arn
task_role_arn            = data.aws_iam_role.lab.arn

container_definitions = jsonencode([{
name      = "bank-api-nodejs"
image     = "${aws_ecr_repository.services["bank-api-nodejs"].repository_url}:${var.image_tag}"
essential = true

     portMappings = [{ containerPort = 3000, hostPort = 3000, protocol = "tcp" }]

     environment = [
       { name = "PORT", value = "3000" },
     ]
     secrets = [
       { name = "MONGO_URI",  valueFrom = local.bank_api_mongo_uri_secret },
       { name = "TOKEN_KEY",  valueFrom = local.bank_api_token_key_secret },
     ]

     healthCheck = {
       command     = ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:3000/health || exit 1"]
       interval    = 10
       timeout     = 5
       retries     = 2
       startPeriod = 30
     }

     logConfiguration = local.log_config["bank-api-nodejs"]
}])

depends_on = [docker_registry_image.services]
}

Add ECS service (no ALB — internal only):
resource "aws_ecs_service" "bank_api_nodejs" {
name            = "bank-api-nodejs"
cluster         = aws_ecs_cluster.spendsmart.id
task_definition = aws_ecs_task_definition.bank_api_nodejs.arn
desired_count   = 1
launch_type     = "FARGATE"

network_configuration {
subnets          = data.aws_subnets.default.ids
security_groups  = [aws_security_group.ecs.id]
assign_public_ip = true
}

service_registries {
registry_arn = aws_service_discovery_service.internal["bank-api-nodejs"].arn
}
}

3c. terraform/ecs.tf — inject BANK_API_BASE_URL into dependent services

Update aws_ecs_task_definition.bank_auth_service environment:
{ name = "BANK_API_BASE_URL", value = "http://bank-api-nodejs.spendsmart.local:3000" }

Update aws_ecs_task_definition.banking_service environment:
{ name = "BANK_API_BASE_URL", value = "http://bank-api-nodejs.spendsmart.local:3000" }

 ---
Part 4 — banking-service Java changes

4a. New DTO: dto/BankApiTransaction.java

Maps the Node.js transaction JSON fields: _id, transactionType, accountNumber, transactionAmount, transactionTime.

4b. New client: client/BankApiNodeJsClient.java

Injected with @Qualifier("bankApiRestClient"). Two methods:
1. getAccountNumber(token) — decodes the BankApiNodeJs JWT (base64url split on ., decode payload, read user_id), calls GET /api/user/{user_id}, returns the accountNumber long.
2. getTransactions(accountNumber) — calls GET /api/transaction/{accountNumber}, returns List<BankApiTransaction>.

JWT decode is just payload parsing (no verification) — split on ., base64url-decode index 1, parse user_id with ObjectMapper. Add padding with "=".repeat((4 - s.length() % 4) % 4).

4c. Update adapter/BankApiAdapter.java

Add BankApiNodeJsClient field (use @RequiredArgsConstructor). Implement fetchTransactions:
@Override
public List<NormalisedTransaction> fetchTransactions(String token, String userId) {
long accountNumber = bankApiNodeJsClient.getAccountNumber(token);
return bankApiNodeJsClient.getTransactions(accountNumber).stream()
.map(t -> toNormalised(t, userId))
.collect(Collectors.toList());
}
Map: amount = abs(transactionAmount), currency = "NGN", occurredAt parsed from transactionTime ISO string, externalTxnId = _id.

4d. Update config/RestClientConfig.java

Add:
@Value("${bankapi.base-url}")
private String bankApiBaseUrl;

@Bean("bankApiRestClient")
public RestClient bankApiRestClient(RestClient.Builder builder) {
return builder.baseUrl(bankApiBaseUrl).build();
}

4e. Update application.properties

bankapi.base-url=${BANK_API_BASE_URL:http://localhost:3000}

4f. Update application-local.properties

bankapi.base-url=http://localhost:3000

 ---
Part 5 — Secrets setup (manual, pre-deploy)

Before running terraform apply, create a Secrets Manager secret with two keys:
- mongo_uri — MongoDB Atlas connection string (e.g. mongodb+srv://...)
- token_key — the JWT signing secret used by BankApiNodeJs

MongoDB Atlas free tier (M0) is the recommended choice — create a cluster, whitelist 0.0.0.0/0 (or the ECS subnet CIDRs), and store the connection string in the secret.

 ---
Verification

Local (before ECS deploy)

● The full flow works end-to-end. Here's what just happened:

1. POST /api/v1/login/bankapi → HTTP 200 — bank-auth-service called BankApiNodeJs /api/login, got the JWT back, stored it in memory under "local-test-user"
2. GET /api/v1/banking/transactions → real transaction data:
   - banking-service called bank-auth-service to retrieve the stored JWT
   - BankApiAdapter decoded the JWT to extract user_id
   - Called GET /api/user/{user_id} → got accountNumber: 8588860
   - Called GET /api/transaction/8588860 → got the deposit transaction
   - Mapped it to NormalisedTransaction with provider: "bankapi", currency: "NGN", amount: 5000
   M services/banking-service/src/main/java/com/spendmart/banking_service/adapter/BankApiAdapter.java
   M services/banking-service/src/main/java/com/spendmart/banking_service/config/RestClientConfig.java
   M services/banking-service/src/main/java/com/spendmart/banking_service/config/SecurityConfig.java
   M services/banking-service/src/main/java/com/spendmart/banking_service/controller/BankingController.java

   3a. terraform/ecr.tf — add to service_names

   locals {
   service_names = [
   "expense-service",
   "banking-service",
   "query-service",
   "alerts-service",
   "bank-auth-service",
   "group-service",
   "bank-api-nodejs",   # ← add
   ]
   }
   This automatically creates: ECR repo, Docker image build/push, CloudWatch log group, log_config entry.

   3b. terraform/ecs.tf — add to internal_services and add task definition + service

   Add to local.internal_services:
   "bank-api-nodejs" = 3000
   This creates the Cloud Map DNS entry: bank-api-nodejs.spendsmart.local.

   Add a new Secrets Manager secret reference local for the MongoDB URI and BankApi token key:
   bank_api_mongo_uri_secret  = "${aws_secretsmanager_secret.bank_api.arn}:mongo_uri::"
   bank_api_token_key_secret  = "${aws_secretsmanager_secret.bank_api.arn}:token_key::"

   Add a new aws_secretsmanager_secret.bank_api resource in terraform/secrets.tf (or ecs.tf) to hold MONGO_URI and TOKEN_KEY.

   Add ECS task definition:
   resource "aws_ecs_task_definition" "bank_api_nodejs" {
   family                   = "spendsmart-bank-api-nodejs"
   network_mode             = "awsvpc"
   requires_compatibilities = ["FARGATE"]
   cpu                      = 256
   memory                   = 512
   execution_role_arn       = data.aws_iam_role.lab.arn
   task_role_arn            = data.aws_iam_role.lab.arn

   container_definitions = jsonencode([{
   name      = "bank-api-nodejs"
   image     = "${aws_ecr_repository.services["bank-api-nodejs"].repository_url}:${var.image_tag}"
   essential = true

       portMappings = [{ containerPort = 3000, hostPort = 3000, protocol = "tcp" }]

       environment = [
         { name = "PORT", value = "3000" },
       ]
       secrets = [
         { name = "MONGO_URI",  valueFrom = local.bank_api_mongo_uri_secret },
         { name = "TOKEN_KEY",  valueFrom = local.bank_api_token_key_secret },
       ]

       healthCheck = {
         command     = ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:3000/health || exit 1"]
         interval    = 10
         timeout     = 5
         retries     = 2
         startPeriod = 30
       }

       logConfiguration = local.log_config["bank-api-nodejs"]
   }])

   depends_on = [docker_registry_image.services]
   }

   Add ECS service (no ALB — internal only):
   resource "aws_ecs_service" "bank_api_nodejs" {
   name            = "bank-api-nodejs"
   cluster         = aws_ecs_cluster.spendsmart.id
   task_definition = aws_ecs_task_definition.bank_api_nodejs.arn
   desired_count   = 1
   launch_type     = "FARGATE"

   network_configuration {
   subnets          = data.aws_subnets.default.ids
   security_groups  = [aws_security_group.ecs.id]
   assign_public_ip = true
   }

   service_registries {
   registry_arn = aws_service_discovery_service.internal["bank-api-nodejs"].arn
   }
   }

   3c. terraform/ecs.tf — inject BANK_API_BASE_URL into dependent services

   Update aws_ecs_task_definition.bank_auth_service environment:
   { name = "BANK_API_BASE_URL", value = "http://bank-api-nodejs.spendsmart.local:3000" }

   Update aws_ecs_task_definition.banking_service environment:
   { name = "BANK_API_BASE_URL", value = "http://bank-api-nodejs.spendsmart.local:3000" }

   ---
   Part 4 — banking-service Java changes

   4a. New DTO: dto/BankApiTransaction.java

   Maps the Node.js transaction JSON fields: _id, transactionType, accountNumber, transactionAmount, transactionTime.

   4b. New client: client/BankApiNodeJsClient.java

   Injected with @Qualifier("bankApiRestClient"). Two methods:
    1. getAccountNumber(token) — decodes the BankApiNodeJs JWT (base64url split on ., decode payload, read user_id), calls GET /api/user/{user_id}, returns the accountNumber long.
    2. getTransactions(accountNumber) — calls GET /api/transaction/{accountNumber}, returns List<BankApiTransaction>.

   JWT decode is just payload parsing (no verification) — split on ., base64url-decode index 1, parse user_id with ObjectMapper. Add padding with "=".repeat((4 - s.length() % 4) % 4).

   4c. Update adapter/BankApiAdapter.java

   Add BankApiNodeJsClient field (use @RequiredArgsConstructor). Implement fetchTransactions:
   @Override
   public List<NormalisedTransaction> fetchTransactions(String token, String userId) {
   long accountNumber = bankApiNodeJsClient.getAccountNumber(token);
   return bankApiNodeJsClient.getTransactions(accountNumber).stream()
   .map(t -> toNormalised(t, userId))
   .collect(Collectors.toList());
   }
   Map: amount = abs(transactionAmount), currency = "NGN", occurredAt parsed from transactionTime ISO string, externalTxnId = _id.

   4d. Update config/RestClientConfig.java

   Add:
   @Value("${bankapi.base-url}")
   private String bankApiBaseUrl;

   @Bean("bankApiRestClient")
   public RestClient bankApiRestClient(RestClient.Builder builder) {
   return builder.baseUrl(bankApiBaseUrl).build();
   }

   4e. Update application.properties

   bankapi.base-url=${BANK_API_BASE_URL:http://localhost:3000}

   4f. Update application-local.properties

   bankapi.base-url=http://localhost:3000

   ---
   Part 5 — Secrets setup (manual, pre-deploy)

   Before running terraform apply, create a Secrets Manager secret with two keys:
    - mongo_uri — MongoDB Atlas connection string (e.g. mongodb+srv://...)
    - token_key — the JWT signing secret used by BankApiNodeJs

   MongoDB Atlas free tier (M0) is the recommended choice — create a cluster, whitelist 0.0.0.0/0 (or the ECS subnet CIDRs), and store the connection string in the secret.

   ---
   Verification

   Local (before ECS deploy)

    1. Start MongoDB + BankApiNodeJs: node index.js from services/bank-api-nodejs/
    2. Start bank-auth-service: ./gradlew bootRun --args='--spring.profiles.active=local'
    3. Start banking-service: ./gradlew bootRun --args='--spring.profiles.active=local'
    4. Register/login a BankApiNodeJs user, deposit funds via POST http://localhost:3000/api/deposit
    5. Call POST http://localhost:8087/api/v1/login/bankapi with { "username": "...", "password": "..." }
    6. Call GET http://localhost:8083/api/v1/banking/transactions — expect transaction array with provider: "bankapi"

   ECS (after deploy)

    1. terraform apply from terraform/ directory
    2. Check ECS console — bank-api-nodejs service should reach RUNNING state
    3. Verify Cloud Map has bank-api-nodejs.spendsmart.local registered
    4. Hit the ALB: POST {alb}/api/v1/login/bankapi → then GET {alb}/api/v1/banking/transactions

- secrets.tf — added spendsmart/bank-api Secrets Manager secret for MONGO_URI and TOKEN_KEY
- variables.tf — added bank_api_mongo_uri (required) and bank_api_token_key variables

● The full flow works end-to-end. Here's what just happened:

1. POST /api/v1/login/bankapi → HTTP 200 — bank-auth-service called BankApiNodeJs /api/login, got the JWT back, stored it in memory under "local-test-user"

   - BankApiAdapter decoded the JWT to extract user_id
   - Called GET /api/user/{user_id} → got accountNumber: 8588860
   - Called GET /api/transaction/8588860 → got the deposit transaction
   - Mapped it to NormalisedTransaction with provider: "bankapi", currency: "NGN", amount: 5000

     { name = "BANK_API_BASE_URL", value = "http://bank-api-nodejs.spendsmart.local:3000" }

     ---
     Part 4 — banking-service Java changes

     4a. New DTO: dto/BankApiTransaction.java

     Maps the Node.js transaction JSON fields: _id, transactionType, accountNumber, transactionAmount, transactionTime.

     4b. New client: client/BankApiNodeJsClient.java

     Injected with @Qualifier("bankApiRestClient"). Two methods:
     1. getAccountNumber(token) — decodes the BankApiNodeJs JWT (base64url split on ., decode payload, read user_id), calls GET /api/user/{user_id}, returns the accountNumber long.
     2. getTransactions(accountNumber) — calls GET /api/transaction/{accountNumber}, returns List<BankApiTransaction>.

     JWT decode is just payload parsing (no verification) — split on ., base64url-decode index 1, parse user_id with ObjectMapper. Add padding with "=".repeat((4 - s.length() % 4) % 4).

     4c. Update adapter/BankApiAdapter.java

     Add BankApiNodeJsClient field (use @RequiredArgsConstructor). Implement fetchTransactions:
     @Override
     public List<NormalisedTransaction> fetchTransactions(String token, String userId) {
         long accountNumber = bankApiNodeJsClient.getAccountNumber(token);
         return bankApiNodeJsClient.getTransactions(accountNumber).stream()
                 .map(t -> toNormalised(t, userId))
                 .collect(Collectors.toList());
     }
     Map: amount = abs(transactionAmount), currency = "NGN", occurredAt parsed from transactionTime ISO string, externalTxnId = _id.

     4d. Update config/RestClientConfig.java

     Add:
     @Value("${bankapi.base-url}")
     private String bankApiBaseUrl;

     @Bean("bankApiRestClient")
     public RestClient bankApiRestClient(RestClient.Builder builder) {
         return builder.baseUrl(bankApiBaseUrl).build();
     }

     4e. Update application.properties

     bankapi.base-url=${BANK_API_BASE_URL:http://localhost:3000}

     4f. Update application-local.properties

     bankapi.base-url=http://localhost:3000

     ---
     Part 5 — Secrets setup (manual, pre-deploy)

     Before running terraform apply, create a Secrets Manager secret with two keys:
     - mongo_uri — MongoDB Atlas connection string (e.g. mongodb+srv://...)
     - token_key — the JWT signing secret used by BankApiNodeJs

     MongoDB Atlas free tier (M0) is the recommended choice — create a cluster, whitelist 0.0.0.0/0 (or the ECS subnet CIDRs), and store the connection string in the secret.

     ---
     Verification

     Local (before ECS deploy)

     1. Start MongoDB + BankApiNodeJs: node index.js from services/bank-api-nodejs/
     2. Start bank-auth-service: ./gradlew bootRun --args='--spring.profiles.active=local'
     3. Start banking-service: ./gradlew bootRun --args='--spring.profiles.active=local'
     4. Register/login a BankApiNodeJs user, deposit funds via POST http://localhost:3000/api/deposit
     5. Call POST http://localhost:8087/api/v1/login/bankapi with { "username": "...", "password": "..." }
     6. Call GET http://localhost:8083/api/v1/banking/transactions — expect transaction array with provider: "bankapi"

     ECS (after deploy)

     1. terraform apply from terraform/ directory
     2. Check ECS console — bank-api-nodejs service should reach RUNNING state
     3. Verify Cloud Map has bank-api-nodejs.spendsmart.local registered
     4. Hit the ALB: POST {alb}/api/v1/login/bankapi → then GET {alb}/api/v1/banking/transactions

● Clean compile — no errors. Here's a summary of everything that was done:

  ---
Part 1 — services/bank-api-nodejs/ (moved from BankApiNodeJs/, nested .git removed):
- index.js — added GET /health endpoint for ECS health checks
- Dockerfile — Node 20 Alpine, production deps only, exposes port 3000
- .dockerignore — excludes node_modules, .env, .git

Part 2 — banking-service Java (4 files new/modified):
- dto/BankApiTransaction.java — maps _id, transactionType, transactionAmount, transactionTime from Node response
- client/BankApiNodeJsClient.java — decodes stored JWT to extract user_id, calls GET /api/user/{id} for account number, then GET /api/transaction/{accountNumber}
- adapter/BankApiAdapter.java — implemented fetchTransactions() using the client; maps to NormalisedTransaction with currency="NGN"
- config/RestClientConfig.java + application.properties + application-local.properties — adds bankApiRestClient bean and bankapi.base-url property

Part 3 — Terraform (4 files):
- ecr.tf — added "bank-api-nodejs" to service_names (auto-creates ECR repo + Docker build)
- ecs.tf — added "bank-api-nodejs" = 3000 to internal_services (Cloud Map DNS); added BANK_API_BASE_URL env var to banking-service and bank-auth-service task defs; added new task definition + ECS service with container health check
- secrets.tf — added spendsmart/bank-api Secrets Manager secret for MONGO_URI and TOKEN_KEY
- variables.tf — added bank_api_mongo_uri (required) and bank_api_token_key variables

Before running terraform apply, you'll need a MongoDB Atlas M0 cluster and pass: terraform apply -var="bank_api_mongo_uri=mongodb+srv://...".

● Committed. Here are the handover notes:
  
---
Handover: BankApiNodeJs → ECS Integration

What was done

BankApiNodeJs (Node.js/Express/MongoDB bank API) is now a first-class service in the project. The banking-service can fetch real transaction data from it, and it's fully wired into the Terraform ECS deployment.

  ---
How the flow works

POST /api/v1/login/bankapi  →  bank-auth-service
calls BankApiNodeJs POST /api/login, stores JWT in DynamoDB keyed (cognitoUserId, "bankapi")

GET /api/v1/banking/transactions  →  banking-service
1. retrieves stored JWT from bank-auth-service
2. decodes JWT payload → extracts MongoDB user_id
3. GET /api/user/{user_id}      → gets accountNumber
4. GET /api/transaction/{acct}  → gets transactions
5. returns normalised list with provider="bankapi", currency="NGN"

  ---

  ---
Running locally

Prerequisites: Docker running (for MongoDB)

# MongoDB (if not already running)
docker run -d --name mongodb -p 27017:27017 mongo:6

# bank-api-nodejs (from project root)
cd services/bank-api-nodejs
# create .env with: MONGO_URI=mongodb://localhost:27017/bankapi  TOKEN_KEY=any-secret  PORT=3000
node index.js

# bank-auth-service
cd services/bank-auth-service
./gradlew bootRun --args='--spring.profiles.active=local'

# banking-service
cd services/banking-service
./gradlew bootRun --args='--spring.profiles.active=local'

Test it:
# 1. Register a BankApiNodeJs user (first time only)
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/register \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-d '{"fullName":"Test","email":"test@example.com","password":"password123","accountBalance":10000}'

# 2. Deposit to create a transaction (first time only)
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/deposit \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-d '{"accountNumber":<from register response>,"depositAmount":5000,"description":"Test","from":"Me"}'

# 3. Connect account via bank-auth-service
curl -X POST http://localhost:8087/api/v1/login/bankapi \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-d '{"email":"test@example.com","password":"password123"}'

# 4. Fetch transactions
curl http://localhost:8083/api/v1/banking/transactions

  ---
Before deploying to ECS

1. MongoDB Atlas — create a free M0 cluster, get the connection string
2. terraform.tfvars — add:
   bank_api_mongo_uri = "mongodb+srv://user:pass@cluster.mongodb.net/bankapi"
   bank_api_token_key = "your-jwt-secret"   # same value used in bank-api-nodejs .env
   enable_service_discovery = true
3. Run terraform apply from terraform/ — this builds + pushes the bank-api-nodejs Docker image to ECR and starts the ECS service

❯ ok lets go through testing the BankApiNodeJs again: Handover: BankApiNodeJs → ECS Integration

    What was done                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    
    BankApiNodeJs (Node.js/Express/MongoDB bank API) is now a first-class service in the project. The banking-service can fetch real transaction data from it, and it's fully wired into the Terraform ECS deployment.                              
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    
    ---                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             
    How the flow works                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    
    POST /api/v1/login/bankapi  →  bank-auth-service                                                                                                                                                                                                
      calls BankApiNodeJs POST /api/login, stores JWT in DynamoDB keyed (cognitoUserId, "bankapi")                                                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    
    GET /api/v1/banking/transactions  →  banking-service                                                                                                                                                                                            
      1. retrieves stored JWT from bank-auth-service                                                                                                                                                                                                
      2. decodes JWT payload → extracts MongoDB user_id                                                                                                                                                                                             
      3. GET /api/user/{user_id}      → gets accountNumber                                                                                                                                                                                          
      4. GET /api/transaction/{acct}  → gets transactions                                                                                                                                                                                           
      5. returns normalised list with provider="bankapi", currency="NGN"

    Before deploying to ECS                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    
    1. MongoDB Atlas — create a free M0 cluster, get the connection string                                                                                                                                                                          
    2. terraform.tfvars — add:                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
    bank_api_mongo_uri = "mongodb+srv://user:pass@cluster.mongodb.net/bankapi"                                                                                                                                                                      
    bank_api_token_key = "your-jwt-secret"   # same value used in bank-api-nodejs .env                                                                                                                                                              
    enable_service_discovery = true                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
    3. Run terraform apply from terraform/ — this builds + pushes the bank-api-nodejs Docker image to ECR and starts the ECS service. I just want to make sure it works with the banking service

❯ now what happens why I deploy and use cognito and stuff. Will it still work

● Good question. In production (with Cognito), the flow changes in one key way — the jwt parameter in the controllers will be a real Cognito JWT instead of null. Here's what happens at each step:

What changes:

┌────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    │                Local                 │              Production (ECS + Cognito)              │                                                                                                            
├────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ jwt in controllers │ null → defaults to "local-test-user" │ Real Cognito JWT, jwt.getSubject() = Cognito user ID │
├────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Token storage key  │ "local-test-user"                    │ Actual Cognito user ID (e.g. "abc-123-xyz")          │
├────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ TokenStore         │ In-memory (LocalTokenStore)          │ DynamoDB                                             │
├────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Security           │ All requests permitted               │ Must have valid Cognito Bearer token                 │
└────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

What stays the same:
- The POST /api/v1/login/bankapi call is identical — just needs a Cognito Bearer token in the header
- The JWT stored in DynamoDB is still the BankApiNodeJs JWT
- The transaction fetching logic in BankApiAdapter is unchanged

The one risk — token lookup mismatch:

In local, you stored the BankApiNodeJs JWT under "local-test-user". In production, it gets stored under the real Cognito user ID. As long as the user calls POST /api/v1/login/bankapi with their Cognito token before calling GET
/api/v1/banking/transactions, it will work correctly.

If they hit /transactions without having logged in first, BankAuthClient.getToken() returns empty → BankingService returns []. That's the expected behaviour — same as OBP.

So yes, it will work in production as-is. No code changes needed.

❯ can we test depositing and withdrawing money or something like that

● The banking-service is read-only (only fetches transactions), so deposits and withdrawals go directly to BankApiNodeJs on port 3000. The interesting test is then seeing those new transactions show up via banking-service afterwards.

Here's the sequence:

Step 1 — Login to BankApiNodeJs directly to get a JWT (needed for withdraw):
curl.exe -s -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/login \                                                                                                                                                                           
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-d '{"email":"test@example.com","password":"password123"}'
Copy the token field from the response.

Step 2 — Deposit funds (no auth needed):
curl.exe -s -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/deposit \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-d '{"accountNumber":8588860,"depositAmount":5000,"description":"Salary","from":"Employer"}'

Step 3 — Withdraw funds (needs the token from Step 1):
curl.exe -s -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/withdraw \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-H "x-access-token: YOUR_TOKEN_HERE" \
-d '{"withdrawAmount":2000}'

Step 4 — Re-login via bank-auth-service (refreshes the stored JWT):
curl.exe -s -w "\nHTTP %{http_code}" -X POST http://localhost:8087/api/v1/login/bankapi \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-d '{"email":"test@example.com","password":"password123"}'

Step 5 — Fetch all transactions via banking-service:
curl.exe -s http://localhost:8083/api/v1/banking/transactions
You should now see all three transactions (the original deposit + new deposit + withdrawal).

❯ How does the bank-auth-service workflow work currently

● Here's the full picture:
  
---
What bank-auth-service does

It acts as a token broker — it holds credentials for external bank APIs (OBP, BankApiNodeJs) on behalf of each user, so the other services never have to deal with those credentials directly.

  ---
Login flow (storing a token)

User/Frontend
│
│  POST /api/v1/login/bankapi
│  { "email": "...", "password": "..." }
│  Authorization: Bearer <Cognito JWT>
▼
bank-auth-service
│  extracts Cognito user ID from JWT
│  calls BankApiNodeJs POST /api/login
│  gets back BankApiNodeJs JWT
│
▼
DynamoDB (bank-auth-tokens table)
stores: { userId: "cognito-abc", provider: "bankapi", token: "eyJ..." }

  ---
Token retrieval flow (used by banking-service)

banking-service
│
│  GET /api/v1/token/bankapi
│  Authorization: Bearer <Cognito JWT>
▼
bank-auth-service
│  extracts Cognito user ID from JWT
│  looks up DynamoDB: (userId, "bankapi")
│  returns { token: "eyJ..." }
▼
banking-service uses the BankApiNodeJs JWT
to call GET /api/transaction/{accountNumber}

  ---
The two providers side by side

┌──────────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┐
│                                  │               OBP                │       BankApiNodeJs        │
├──────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────┤
│ Login endpoint                   │ POST /api/v1/login/obp           │ POST /api/v1/login/bankapi │
├──────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────┤
│ Credentials sent                 │ username, password, consumer_key │ email, password            │
├──────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────┤
│ Token type stored                │ OBP DirectLogin token            │ BankApiNodeJs JWT          │
├──────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────┤
│ Provider key in DynamoDB         │ "obp"                            │ "bankapi"                  │
├──────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────┤
│ Retrieved by banking-service via │ GET /api/v1/token/obp            │ GET /api/v1/token/bankapi  │
└──────────────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────┘

  ---
Where the BankApiAdapter fits

banking-service receives GET /api/v1/banking/transactions
│
▼
BankingService loops through adapters: [ObpAdapter, BankApiAdapter]
│
│  for each adapter, asks bank-auth-service:
│  "does this user have a token for this provider?"
│
├─ ObpAdapter   → GET /api/v1/token/obp    → 404 (not connected) → skip
└─ BankApiAdapter → GET /api/v1/token/bankapi → 200 + JWT → fetch transactions

So the first adapter that has a stored token wins. If the user has connected both OBP and BankApiNodeJs, OBP wins because it's @Order(1).

  ---
In local dev vs production

- Local: LocalTokenStore (in-memory HashMap), no Cognito — JWT is null so user ID defaults to "local-test-user"
- Production: DynamoDB table bank-auth-tokens, real Cognito JWT required on every request

❯ in the dynamo DB is it stored encrypted. I remember before we were talking about using KMS to encrypt and decrypt tokens. Is that needed

● Let me check the current DynamoDB and TokenStore setup to give you an accurate picture.

Read 2 files (ctrl+o to expand)

● You're already covered. Here's what's in place:

  ---
DynamoDB — KMS encryption at rest is already configured in Terraform:

server_side_encryption {
enabled     = true
kms_key_arn = aws_kms_key.bank_auth_tokens.arn
}

A Customer Managed Key (CMK) with key rotation enabled encrypts everything in the table at rest. AWS handles the encrypt/decrypt transparently when DynamoDB reads/writes — your application code doesn't need to do anything special.

  ---
What this means practically:

┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                        Threat                         │                                Protected?                                 │
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Someone gets access to the raw DynamoDB storage files │ ✓ KMS encryption at rest covers this                                      │
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Someone with DynamoDB read permissions calls GetItem  │ ✓ They also need KMS Decrypt permission on the CMK                        │
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Someone with full AWS console/API access              │ ✗ They can grant themselves KMS access — this is the AWS account boundary │
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Token in transit (DynamoDB ↔ bank-auth-service)       │ ✓ TLS in transit (AWS SDK default)                                        │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  ---
What you don't have (and likely don't need for this project):

Application-level encryption — where TokenStore.java itself calls KMS to encrypt the token string before putting it in DynamoDB. That would protect against someone who has DynamoDB read access but not KMS access. For a university project this
is overkill — the KMS server-side encryption is the right level.

So the short answer: it's already handled, no code changes needed.

  ---
What you don't have (and likely don't need for this project):

Application-level encryption — where TokenStore.java itself calls KMS to encrypt the token string before putting it in DynamoDB. That would protect against someone who has DynamoDB read access but not KMS access. For a university project this
is overkill — the KMS server-side encryption is the right level.

So the short answer: it's already handled, no code changes needed.

Recommended test flow

Phase 1 — Query service (quick win, 5 mins)

The query-service just wraps banking-service with filtering. Same @Profile("!local") bug on its SecurityConfig needs fixing first, then you can test things like:

# All transactions
GET /api/v1/query/transactions

# Filter by provider
GET /api/v1/query/transactions?provider=bankapi

# Filter by amount range
GET /api/v1/query/transactions?minAmount=1000&maxAmount=9000

# Filter by date

Phase 2 — Expense + Settlement flow (the interesting one, 15 mins)

4. POST a settlement linking that transactionId + provider="bankapi" to the expense

❯ just another question. Since we added the local one liner to our services, when they're deployed with the dockerfile and on AWS it doesn't use that profile right?

● Correct — the local profile is never active in production. Here's why:

The Dockerfile:
FROM eclipse-temurin:21-jre-alpine
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=build /app/build/libs/*.jar app.jar                                                                                                                                                                                
ENTRYPOINT ["java", "-jar", "app.jar"]

No -Dspring.profiles.active=local anywhere. Spring Boot defaults to the default profile, so:

- LocalSecurityConfig (@Profile("local")) → never loads
- SecurityConfig (@Profile("!local")) → always loads → Cognito JWT validation is on
- LocalTokenStore (@Profile("local")) → never loads → real TokenStore (DynamoDB) is used
- application-local.properties → ignored → application.properties values used

The only way local could accidentally activate in production is if someone explicitly passed SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=local as an environment variable in the ECS task definition — which none of the Terraform configs do.

So the split is clean:

┌─────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────┐
│             │            Local (IntelliJ)            │      Production (ECS)       │
├─────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────┤
│ Profile     │ local (set manually)                   │ default (implicit)          │
├─────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────┤
│ Security    │ All requests permitted                 │ Cognito JWT required        │
├─────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────┤
│ Token store │ In-memory HashMap                      │ DynamoDB                    │
├─────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────┤
│ Properties  │ application-local.properties overrides │ application.properties only │
└─────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────┘

import com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation.JsonProperty;                                                                                                                                                                                             
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Qualifier;                                                                                                                                                                                    
import org.springframework.http.HttpStatus;                                                                                                                                                                                                       
import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;                                                                                                                                                                                                  
import org.springframework.web.client.HttpClientErrorException;                                                                                                                                                                                   
import org.springframework.web.client.ResourceAccessException;                                                                                                                                                                                    
import org.springframework.web.client.RestClient;                                                                                                                                                                                                 
import org.springframework.web.server.ResponseStatusException;

import java.util.Optional;

@Component                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
public class BankAuthClient {

      private final RestClient restClient;                                                                                                                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    
      public BankAuthClient(@Qualifier("bankAuthRestClient") RestClient restClient) {                                                                                                                                                               
          this.restClient = restClient;                                                                                                                                                                                                             
      }                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    
      public Optional<String> getToken(String cognitoJwt, String provider) {                                                                                                                                                                        
          try {                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
              TokenResponse response = restClient.get()                                                                                                                                                                                             
                      .uri("/api/v1/token/{provider}", provider)                                                                                                                                                                                    
                      .header("Authorization", "Bearer " + cognitoJwt)                                                                                                                                                                              
                      .retrieve()                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
                      .body(TokenResponse.class);                                                                                                                                                                                                   
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    
              if (response == null || response.token() == null) {                                                                                                                                                                                   
                  return Optional.empty();                                                                                                                                                                                                          
              }                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
              return Optional.of(response.token());                                                                                                                                                                                                 
          } catch (HttpClientErrorException.NotFound e) {                                                                                                                                                                                           
              return Optional.empty();                                                                                                                                                                                                              
          } catch (ResourceAccessException e) {                                                                                                                                                                                                     
              throw new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE,                                                                                                                                                                     
                      "bank-auth-service is unreachable");                                                                                                                                                                                          
          }                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
      }                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    
      private record TokenResponse(@JsonProperty("token") String token) {}                                                                                                                                                                          
}                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
See how theres an authorization header. Is the idea of having the !local in the securtiy config that we don't need that for this testing but its needed in prod


In local mode:
- SecurityConfig (@Profile("!local")) doesn't load → no JWT validation anywhere
- All services accept requests with no token, empty token, or anything
- The Authorization: Bearer  header that BankAuthClient sends is completely ignored by bank-auth-service
- @AuthenticationPrincipal Jwt jwt is always null → falls back to "local-test-user"

In production:
- SecurityConfig (@Profile("!local")) loads → Cognito JWT validation is enforced
- Every service-to-service call must carry the real Cognito JWT
- BankAuthClient forwards the user's real Cognito JWT to bank-auth-service
- bank-auth-service validates it, extracts the real Cognito user ID, and looks up DynamoDB for that user's stored token

So the Authorization: Bearer <cognitoJwt> header in BankAuthClient is doing nothing locally but is critical in production — it's how bank-auth-service knows which user's token to look up. Without it, every user would get each other's stored
tokens.

Plan: Bank Authentication Frontend Pages

Context

The frontend already has bank-connect.html (provider selection) and bank-login.html (credentials form), but both are shells with no JavaScript logic. bank-login.html's "Connect" button is just a static <a> link — nothing calls the backend.
This plan wires both pages up to bank-auth-service via the existing api.js client, following the exact patterns used by every other page in the project.

 ---
Architecture

bank-connect.html  →  bank-login.html?provider=bankapi
↓
api.post('/login/bankapi', { email, password })
↓
bank-auth-service POST /api/v1/login/bankapi
↓
localStorage flag: spendsmart.bank.bankapi.connected = true
↓
redirect → home.html

In production, all api.* calls go through the ALB. /api/v1/login/* routes to bank-auth-service automatically. No extra configuration needed.

 ---
Connection state tracking

Since the frontend can't query DynamoDB directly, connection state is tracked in localStorage:
- spendsmart.bank.bankapi.connected = "true" when connected
- spendsmart.bank.obp.connected = "true" when connected

Set on successful login. Cleared on error (so a re-login attempt clears stale state).

 ---
Files to create

frontend/assets/js/pages/bank-connect.js

On load:
- Read localStorage flags for each provider
- Update the status <span class="tag"> elements to show "Connected" (green) or "Disconnected"
- Update button text to "Reconnect" if already connected
- Use nav('bank') to highlight the sidebar item

import { nav } from '../ui.js';

const PROVIDERS = ['bankapi', 'obp'];

nav('bank');

for (const p of PROVIDERS) {
const connected = localStorage.getItem(`spendsmart.bank.${p}.connected`) === 'true';
document.getElementById(`status-${p}`).textContent = connected ? 'Connected' : 'Disconnected';
document.getElementById(`status-${p}`).className = `tag ${connected ? 'ok' : ''}`;
document.getElementById(`btn-${p}`).textContent = connected ? 'Reconnect' : 'Connect';
}

frontend/assets/js/pages/bank-login.js

On load:
- Read ?provider= from query string
- Set page title and show the correct form fields:
    - bankapi → email + password
    - obp → username + password + consumer_key
- On submit:
    - Call api.post('/login/{provider}', credentials)
    - On success: set localStorage flag, show success message, redirect to home.html after 1.5s
    - On error: show error via setStatus

import { api } from '../api.js';
import { nav, setStatus } from '../ui.js';

nav('bank');

const provider = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search).get('provider') || 'bankapi';
// render correct fields, wire submit button

 ---
Files to modify

frontend/bank-connect.html

- Add id attributes to the status tags and buttons so JS can update them:
    - id="status-obp", id="btn-obp", id="status-bankapi", id="btn-bankapi"
- Add <script type="module" src="./assets/js/pages/bank-connect.js"></script> before </body>

frontend/bank-login.html

- Replace the static form with a dynamic layout driven by JS:
    - Keep id="provider-label" for display
    - Add id="fields" div where JS injects the correct inputs
    - Add id="connect-btn" button (real <button>, not <a>)
    - Add id="status" element for feedback
- Add <script type="module" src="./assets/js/pages/bank-login.js"></script> before </body>

Provider-specific fields injected by JS:

bankapi:
<label>Email</label><input id="email" type="email" />
<label>Password</label><input id="password" type="password" />

obp:
<label>Username</label><input id="username" type="text" />
<label>Password</label><input id="password" type="password" />
<label>Consumer Key</label><input id="consumer_key" type="text" />

Credentials built by JS:
// bankapi
{ email: ..., password: ... }

// obp
{ username: ..., password: ..., consumer_key: ... }

API call:
await api.post(`/login/${provider}`, credentials);
localStorage.setItem(`spendsmart.bank.${provider}.connected`, 'true');
setStatus(statusEl, 'ok', 'Connected! Redirecting...');
setTimeout(() => window.location.href = './home.html', 1500);

 ---
Verification

1. Open bank-connect.html — both cards show "Disconnected"
2. Click "Connect BankApi" → goes to bank-login.html?provider=bankapi
3. Enter test@example.com / password123 → click Connect
4. Success message appears, redirects to home.html after 1.5s
5. Go back to bank-connect.html — BankApi card now shows "Connected" tag and "Reconnect" button

● You're correct — the frontend never talks to DynamoDB. That was a poorly worded explanation. Let me clarify:

The problem is: how does bank-connect.html know whether to show "Connected" or "Disconnected" for each provider? There's no existing endpoint that answers "does this user have a stored bank token?". The token is stored in DynamoDB by
bank-auth-service and only ever retrieved internally by banking-service.

So the frontend has two options:

1. localStorage flag (what I proposed) — when the user successfully logs in via bank-login.html, we write spendsmart.bank.bankapi.connected = true in the browser. On bank-connect.html, we just read that flag. The frontend never touches
   DynamoDB — it just remembers what it did.
2. New backend endpoint — add GET /api/v1/token/{provider}/status to bank-auth-service that returns { connected: true/false }. The frontend calls that on page load to get accurate status.

Option 1 is simpler but slightly stale (if the DynamoDB token expires, the frontend still shows "Connected"). Option 2 is accurate but needs a new endpoint.

Which would you prefer?

Plan: Bank Authentication Frontend — bank-login.html

Context

bank-login.html exists as a shell with a static form and no JavaScript. The "Connect" button is a plain <a> link that does nothing. This plan wires it up to bank-auth-service via the existing api.js client. bank-connect.html is left unchanged
— showing connection status is out of scope for this MVP. Unauthenticated queries (e.g. going to search without having logged in first) will receive a backend 404 and surface a friendly error message, which is sufficient for MVP.

 ---

├────────────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤

 ---
bank-login.html changes

- Read ?provider= from query string to set page title and show correct fields
- Replace <a class="btn primary" href="./home.html"> with <button id="connect-btn" class="btn primary">Connect</button>
- Add <p id="status" class="status" hidden></p> for feedback
- Add <script type="module" src="./assets/js/pages/bank-login.js"></script>

Provider-specific fields (rendered by JS into id="fields"):

<input id="f-email" type="email" placeholder="you@example.com" />

 ---
bank-login.js logic

import { api } from '../api.js';
import { nav, setStatus } from '../ui.js';

nav('bank');

const provider = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search).get('provider') ?? 'bankapi';
const statusEl = document.getElementById('status');

// Set title
document.getElementById('provider-label').textContent = provider;

// Inject correct fields
const fields = document.getElementById('fields');
if (provider === 'bankapi') {
fields.innerHTML = `...email + password inputs...`;
} else {
fields.innerHTML = `...username + password + consumer_key inputs...`;
}

// Submit
document.getElementById('connect-btn').addEventListener('click', async () => {
const btn = document.getElementById('connect-btn');
btn.disabled = true;

const credentials = provider === 'bankapi'
? { email: fields.querySelector('#f-email').value.trim(),
password: fields.querySelector('#f-password').value }
: { username: fields.querySelector('#f-username').value.trim(),
password: fields.querySelector('#f-password').value,
consumer_key: fields.querySelector('#f-consumer-key').value.trim() };

try {
await api.post(`/login/${provider}`, credentials);
setStatus(statusEl, 'ok', 'Connected! Redirecting…');
setTimeout(() => { window.location.href = './home.html'; }, 1500);
} catch (err) {
setStatus(statusEl, 'err', err.message ?? 'Login failed. Check your credentials.');
btn.disabled = false;
}
});

---

❯ for the group service should the member management be in group service or a separate service

⏺ Keep it in group-service. Here is why:

Group membership is tightly coupled to group identity — you cannot add a member without a group existing, you cannot validate an expense split without checking group membership. Separating them would mean either:

1. A member-service that the group-service calls synchronously (extra network hop, temporal coupling), or
2. A member-service that publishes events (adds broker complexity)

Neither is worth it at this scale. The rule of thumb is: if two things always change together and always need each other to validate, they belong in the same service.

The pattern expense-service already uses (GroupMemberRepository directly in ExpenseService) only works because group and expense share the same database. If you split member management out you lose that.

Recommendation: GroupController handles both group CRUD and member add/remove under /api/v1/groups/{id}/members. Single deployable, single transaction boundary.

---

❯ should addMember accept a userId UUID or an email address

⏺ UUID is simpler and more consistent with the rest of the system, but email is more usable from a frontend perspective. Trade-offs:

UUID approach
- Consistent with how every other entity references users (expense splits, group ownership all use UUID)
- No extra lookup needed — just parse and use
- Downside: the person inviting needs to know the other user's UUID, which is not user-friendly

Email approach
- User friendly — type an email to invite someone
- Requires a lookup: email → UUID before you can persist the GroupMember
- Adds a UserRepository dependency to GroupService
- What happens if the email does not exist yet? You either fail or create a placeholder user

For an MVP where users are identified by Cognito sub (UUID), go with UUID for now. The UserRepository lookup can be added later when you wire up a proper invite flow. Keep it consistent with the rest of the codebase.

---

❯ what is the right way to handle soft delete for groups, set active false or actually delete

⏺ Soft delete (set active = false) is the right call here for a few reasons:

1. Referential integrity — expenses and settlements reference the group. Hard deleting a group would require cascading deletes across expenses, shares, and settlements, which is destructive and hard to reverse.

2. Audit trail — if a group is deleted and a user disputes a settlement, you want the historical record to still exist.

3. Consistency — the GroupMember entity already has an active flag for deactivating members. Using the same pattern on Group keeps the codebase consistent.

Implementation: add active boolean to Group entity (default true), filter all queries with andActiveTrue, and expose DELETE /api/v1/groups/{id} as a soft delete that sets active = false and deactivates all members.

One thing to watch: expense-service checks group membership via GroupMemberRepository directly. Make sure it only reads active members — existsByGroup_IdAndUser_IdAndActiveTrue already does this, so you are covered.

@Test
void create_succeeds_andPublishesEvent() {
// Arrange: caller is active member, split balances, all split users are active members
when(groupMemberRepository.existsByGroup_IdAndUser_IdAndActiveTrue(groupId, callerId)).thenReturn(true);
when(groupMemberRepository.countByGroup_IdAndUser_IdInAndActiveTrue(any(), any())).thenReturn(1L);
when(entityManager.getReference(User.class, callerId)).thenReturn(mockUser);
when(entityManager.getReference(Group.class, groupId)).thenReturn(mockGroup);
when(expenseRepository.save(any())).thenAnswer(inv -> {
Expense e = inv.getArgument(0);
e.setId(UUID.randomUUID()); e.setVersion(0L); return e;
});

      ExpenseResponse resp = expenseService.create(callerId, request);

      assertThat(resp.getAmount()).isEqualByComparingTo(BigDecimal.TEN);
      verify(expenseEventPublisher).expenseCreated(any());
}

@Test
void update_succeeds_whenVersionMatches_andPublishesEvent() {
// Arrange: caller owns expense, version matches, no settlements
when(expenseRepository.findById(expenseId)).thenReturn(Optional.of(expenseAtVersion(0L)));
when(settlementRepository.existsByExpense_Id(expenseId)).thenReturn(false);
when(groupMemberRepository.existsByGroup_IdAndUser_IdAndActiveTrue(any(), any())).thenReturn(true);
when(groupMemberRepository.countByGroup_IdAndUser_IdInAndActiveTrue(any(), any())).thenReturn(1L);
when(expenseRepository.save(any())).thenAnswer(inv -> inv.getArgument(0));

      request.setVersion(0L);
      expenseService.update(expenseId, callerId, request);

      verify(expenseEventPublisher).expenseUpdated(any());
}

@Test
void update_throws409_whenSettlementsExist() {
when(expenseRepository.findById(expenseId)).thenReturn(Optional.of(expenseAtVersion(0L)));
when(settlementRepository.existsByExpense_Id(expenseId)).thenReturn(true);
request.setVersion(0L);

      assertThrows(ConflictException.class, () -> expenseService.update(expenseId, callerId, request));
}

@Test
void delete_succeeds_andPublishesEvent() {
when(expenseRepository.findById(expenseId)).thenReturn(Optional.of(expenseAtVersion(0L)));

      expenseService.delete(expenseId, callerId, 0L);

      verify(settlementRepository).deleteByExpense_Id(expenseId);
      verify(shareRepository).deleteByExpense_Id(expenseId);
      verify(expenseRepository).delete(any());
      verify(expenseEventPublisher).expenseDeleted(any());
}

void getById_throws403_whenCallerNotGroupMember() {
Expense expense = expenseAtVersion(0L);

when(groupMemberRepository.existsByGroup_IdAndUser_IdAndActiveTrue(groupId, callerId)).thenReturn(false);

      assertThrows(ForbiddenException.class, () -> expenseService.getById(expenseId, callerId));
}

when(groupMemberRepository.existsByGroup_IdAndUser_IdAndActiveTrue(any(), any())).thenReturn(true);

@SpringBootTest

class ExpenseServiceIT {

      @Autowired ExpenseService expenseService;
      @Autowired UserRepository userRepository;
      @Autowired GroupRepository groupRepository;
      @Autowired GroupMemberRepository groupMemberRepository;
      @Autowired ExpenseRepository expenseRepository;

      // seed a user, group, membership before each test

      @Test
      void create_thenUpdate_incrementsVersion() {
          // create at version 0, update returns version 1
      }

      @Test
      void concurrentUpdates_secondThrowsConflict() {
          // Create expense. Load it twice. Update from first load (succeeds, now version=1).
          // Try to update with the stale version=0 → ConflictException.
          // This proves the version check catches stale writes.
      }

      @Test
      void delete_withStaleVersion_throwsConflict() {
          // create, then try to delete with version=1 when it's at version=0
      }
}
